Last winter I posted a really sad old song on my story. Rain, piano, lyrics about someone who's gone. I didn't think about it.
Within an hour, Kiran messaged: "Hey, just checking. You okay? Or is it just a good song? 🙂"
I smiled at my phone. It was just a good song. Well, mostly. It was the song my old school played at our farewell, and I was missing those friends a bit. Nostalgia, not a crisis.
I told Kiran exactly that.
Kiran wrote, "Okay! Glad you're okay. Miss them with you."
What I liked was how Kiran asked. No big panic. No "are you depressed??" in front of everyone. Just a small, kind question that let me say either way.
A different friend commented publicly, "Who hurt you?" with a crying face. That felt weird.
One post doesn't tell you much. A quiet check-in tells you more.
- Ojas

Counsellor's note - Kavitha, Friday
Two teachers came to me worried: Keerthana in Class 10 had posted five very sad songs in a row on her public playlist this week. One of them wondered if she was in trouble at home.
I did not call her in as if it were a crisis. At lunch I found her in the library and said, "I noticed your playlist this week. How are you doing?"
She laughed, surprised. "Oh! That's for our dance project. We're choreographing a piece about loss. We picked the saddest songs we could find."
I believed her. But I also said, "If a sad song ever does match your mood, you can come and sit here. No reason needed."
She smiled and showed me a video of their rehearsal.
I told the teachers it was a project. One post, or five, is a cue to check kindly, not a conclusion.

qa.a: Five very sad songs in a row.

qa.a: It was brief, private and calm, asking how Keerthana was instead of assuming a crisis, while still offering support if she needed it.

Wednesday
Varun bhaiya broke up with Nisha last week, and since then he's posted four dance-trend videos. Goofy ones. Him in the kitchen doing the chicken-arm thing with Dadi's dupatta.
Mummy says, "See, he's fine, he's dancing." Chachi says, "He's hiding it, poor boy."
I don't know. Maybe both. Maybe it's just the trend everyone's doing.
So tonight I knocked on his door. I said, "Your videos are hilarious. Also, how are you actually?"
He laughed. Then he sat on the bed and said, "Honestly? Half fine. The dancing helps. The nights are bad."
We sat for a bit. I told him he could come to my room anytime and watch terrible films.
One video didn't tell me he was fine or not fine. Asking did.
- Ayesha
